name: plane_soft_rubber_constant_friction_5n
parameter_origin: Illustrative synthetic values; not measured properties of a named commercial material.
material_label: Soft rubber-like solid, constant Coulomb friction at 5 N
model_notes: Load-controlled at 5 N; travel is an outcome.

Constant Coulomb friction. Velocity weakening gives dmu/dv < 0, so a point that starts sliding loses friction and slides more. That positive feedback sits on top of the zero-pressure points the footprint perimeter always carries, whose friction capacity is mu*p = 0 and which therefore flip between open, sliding and sticking as soon as shear is applied. Removing the feedback makes those flips benign.
The 0.60/0.45 pair it replaces is synthetic: the shared suite records its parameter_origin as illustrative, not measured.
